topic: Concurrency and Sync Primitives for Predictable Behavior
explanation: Concurrency arises when multiple threads execute seemingly simultaneously, sharing resources like memory.  Synchronization primitives are mechanisms that ensure correct and predictable behavior when multiple threads access shared resources concurrently, preventing race conditions and data corruption.  In computer architecture, this requires careful management of CPU scheduling, memory access, and cache coherence.
